# Challenger House

> Organisational Architecture for the AI transition. Nobody wrote down how you lead. Every function in your company is being redesigned for AI, except the one that runs them all: management. That gap is the missing middle, and Challenger House builds it with your leadership team, on real work, live.

The site has three pages beyond this landing summary. The landing page says why. What we do says what. How we think is the full reference, in seven parts, for anyone who wants to chew.

We are three builders (Marcus Druen, André Cramer, Brittney Bean) with three decades of organisational development, facilitation and venture building, now turned on the AI transition. Builders, not consultants. We spark courage to act now.

## Why: the missing middle

You run two organisations: the formal one you wrote down, and the informal one that gets the work done. AI only knows the first. Everything in between is the missing middle, and it has three parts:

- Tacit knowledge: how decisions really get made and where judgment sits. It lives in your best people's heads, and your AI reads the org chart instead.
- Organisational shadow: nobody skipped the writing by accident. Ambiguity protects options, positions and peace. That makes this leadership work, with the team present.
- Learning loop: every pilot reveals something true about how you work. Without a loop, every pilot starts from zero.

AI is coming for the management function. The work below leadership accelerates while the management system still runs on the Monday jour fixe, the hundred-slide deck, the meeting about the meeting. That system was built for an era when talking was how knowledge moved through an organisation. Now knowledge moves through AI, and the talking has a price: the Talking Tax, a live instrument on the landing page.

## What we do (one hour, one day, one quarter)

Full page: https://www.challenger.house/what-we-do

- The hour, free, two visits: 45 minutes with Marcus on the problem that keeps coming back, then an hour one to one with the leader, then an hour inside one of the team's regular meetings with frontier AI on work that looks like theirs.
- [The 1-Day Experience](https://www.challenger.house/what-we-do#one-day): four figures. The leadership team takes one real piece of management work, the board paper, the investment decision, the steering meeting, and rebuilds it with frontier AI, live, in a day. You leave with workflows redesigned, first MVPs, a backlog of use cases, the start of a business case to go beyond Copilot, and a team that has felt what AI does to its own judgment. The most senior accountable leader is in the room.
- [The Build](https://www.challenger.house/what-we-do#build): five figures, one quarter. Three months wrapped around a three-day Residency, on the workflows you actually run: Define (weeks 1 to 4), the Residency (three days), Embed (weeks 5 to 12). You leave with your missing middle built and running, three priority workflows rebuilt with AI inside them, a living Org Mirror, the Writing-Down Protocol, instruments built for your meetings, and board-ready evidence. Zero slide decks.
- [What we are building](https://www.challenger.house/what-we-do#what-we-are-building): the Org Mirror and the AI Constitution, built with pioneering clients.

## Who we work with

Leadership teams who can act on their own authority: a business unit inside a corporation, a standalone subsidiary, a founder-led scale-up. They know the next challenger in their market will be AI-native. They know Copilot is where the race starts. They treat this as a complex change process, 80% people and 20% tools, and lead it themselves.

## Who we are

Full page: https://www.challenger.house/who-we-are

Marcus Druen (Founder, Organisational Architect: he names the elephant), André Cramer (Human & AI Capability Bridge Builder: what AI does to judgment and decision quality; the Plausibility Illusion framework), Brittney Bean (Builder & Coder, Agentic Systems: what the team designs, she makes work, and makes it survive procurement, legal review and IT governance).

## How we think

Full reference: https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think (Organisational Architecture: how AI exposes the organisation you actually run, and what leadership must redesign). Seven parts, thirty-six chapters. Key anchors:

- [The missing middle](https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think#missing-middle): the formal versus the working organisation, the house, the Tower and the Square.
- [The four ways of knowing](https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think#four-ways-of-knowing): why you have to experience AI to lead with it.
- [The five layers](https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think#five-layers): Source, Constitution, Boundaries, Sensorium, Adaptation.
- [The Talking Tax](https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think#talking-tax): information latency, and the cost of chasing, translating and packaging information.
- [AI sovereignty](https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think#ai-sovereignty): governing AI because you understand what you use it for, how far it reaches, what it costs and what it does to judgment. Includes the Plausibility Illusion.
- [The Org Mirror](https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think#org-mirror): reading the working organisation through Morgan, Oshry and Heifetz. An MRI, not surgery.
- [The AI Constitution](https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think#ai-constitution): the CEO writes the manifesto, the leadership team authors the constitution, IT and Legal build the guardrails and open with an AI amnesty. Authored, not downloaded.
- [The instruments](https://www.challenger.house/how-we-think#instruments): Org Mirror, AI Constitution, Delegation Dial, Talking Tax, Attention Constitution, information latency.
